To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

MAM-3 antigen expression is limited to the basal layer of eccrine ducts, and that MAM-6 antigen expression is found in the apical portion of the eccrine secretory canaliculus and in the apical lumena of apocrine acinar and terminal duct cells.

MAM-3 is expressed in the inner layer of the eccrine sweat ducts and that MAM-6 is expressed in the secretory portion of the eccrine acinar cells, in the secretory canalicular cells of the eccrine ducts, and in the sebocytes.

MAM-3 antigen was expressed in the inner layer of normal eccrine ducts, while MAM-6 antigen was expressed within the secretory canals of eccrine acini, and in the terminal ducts, and apical lumina of apocrine acinar cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of MAM antigens, as detected by monoclonal antibody (MoAb) 115D8.
the expression of MAM antigens in the skin appendages and the tumors originating from them.

the immunohistochemical demonstration in normal skin appendages and in benign and malignant tumors of two different antigenic epitopes, MAM-3, which is expressed in the inner layer of eccrine excretary ducts, and MAM- 6, which is expressed by the secretory cells of eccrine and apocrine acini, the terminal portion of eccrine ducts, and the sebocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of MAM antigens is useful as a supplementary marker for the diagnosis of skin appendage tumors, but not as a specific histogenetic marker for any of them.
the expression of the MAM-3/MAM-6 antigents is not useful for a histogenetic diagnosis of skin appendage tumors.
MAM-3 is a useful marker for the differentiation of eccrine ducts and apocrine acini, and MAM- 6 is a marker for the secretory canals of eccrine acini, apocrine acini and sebocytes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the expression of MAM antigens is a feature of the secretory cells in the normal skin appendages and that their expression in the malignant tumors may be explained by a dedifferentiation of the neoplastic epithelium.
the MAM-3 antigen is a specific marker for sweat gland tumors, whereas MAM-6 is a marker for sebaceous gland tumors and for the pilar tumors, although it is not specific for these tumors.
MAM-3 is an eccrine ductal marker and MAM-5 is an apocrine marker.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of MAM antigens in skin appendages is a highly complex and tissue-specific phenomenon.
the MAM-3/MAM-6 antigents are expressed by the inner cells of eccrine excretor ducts and by the apical cells of eccrine sweat glands and apocrine acini, but not by squamous epithelum.
the MAM-3 antigen is expressed by eccrine excretary ducts but not apocrine acini and that MAM-6 is present in both the eccrine acini, apocrine acini, and sebocytes.
